'''Al Mitchell Afalava''' (born January 20, 1987) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Safety (American football position)|safety]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL).  He played [[college football]] for the [[Oregon State Beavers football|Oregon State Beavers]] and was selected by the [[Chicago Bears]] in the sixth round of the [[2009 NFL draft]]. He also played for the [[Indianapolis Colts]] and [[Tennessee Titans]].

==Early life==
Al Afalava was born in [[Lāʻie, Hawaii]], on January 20, 1987.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/alafalava/89682/profile |title=Al Afalava {{!}} NFL.com Player Profile |website=[[NFL.com]] |accessdate=May 16, 2014}}</ref> He played high school football at [[Kahuku High & Intermediate School]]. As a junior, he led Kahuku to a 10-2 record and an appearance in the semifinals of the 2004 state playoffs. The team, ranked No. 14 in the West, won the [[Oahu Interscholastic Association]]. He was named first-team All-State as a senior and led his team to state title and 14-0 record as a junior.<ref name=TennesseeTitansMediaGuideBio>{{cite web |title=Al Afalava {{!}} Tennessee Titans Media Guide Bio |url=http://prod.static.titans.clubs.nfl.com/assets/docs/Afalava_Al_bio.pdf |accessdate=May 16, 2014 |archive-date=May 17, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140517152644/http://prod.static.titans.clubs.nfl.com/assets/docs/Afalava_Al_bio.pdf |url-status=dead}}</ref> He played in the state's Goodwill Football Classic All-Star game and was named a SuperPrep Magazine All-Region team member. As a two-sport athlete, Afalava was given a two-star ranking by Scout.com, which rated him as the second-best defensive back on the Hawaiian Islands.<ref name=CBSSports2015NFLDraftProfile>{{cite web |title=Al Afalava {{!}} CBS Sports 2015 NFL Draft Profile |url=http://www.cbssports.com/nfl/draft/players/historical/565144 |accessdate=May 28, 2014}}</ref>

==College career==
Afalava was the only true-freshman to start for the Oregon State University Beavers Football team in 2005. He missed two games with a knee injury. He made 32 tackles on the season. His six tackles against WSU included a touchdown saving tackle on tight end Troy Bienemann at the 1-yard line. That same game he forced a fumble that set up a go-ahead touchdown. He made eight tackles in the Civil War rivalry game against the Oregon Ducks.<ref name=OSUBeaversBio>{{cite web |title=Al Afalava {{!}} OSUBeavers.com Bio|url=http://www.osubeavers.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=30800&ATCLID=207834248 |accessdate=May 20, 2014 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140521110035/http://www.osubeavers.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=30800&ATCLID=207834248 |archivedate=May 21, 2014 }}</ref>

Afalava started nine times for the Beavers at free safety in 2006, including the last four games. He had 35 tackles for the season. His first career interception came against Arizona State quarterback [[Rudy Carpenter]].<ref name=OSUBeaversBio/> He also forced a fumble against Oregon.<ref name=CBSSports2015NFLDraftProfile/>

In 2007, Afalava was the third-leading tackler on the Beavers football team with 64, including 56 solo tackles. He had a career-high 11 tackles at Arizona State and 10 in the season opener vs. Utah. He recovered two fumbles for the season, both against UCLA, returning one 33 yards in the first quarter for a touchdown.<ref>{{cite web | title=Second Half Comeback Sparks UCLA Victory | website=UCLA Bruins Athletics| date=2007-09-29 | url=https://uclabruins.com/news/2007/9/29/207905876 | access-date=2025-06-22}}</ref> He earned a Pac-10 Honorable Mention.<ref name=OSUBeaversBio/>

In the 2008 season, Afalava recorded 36 tackles, two interceptions, and eight pass break-ups. He was selected to a Pac-10 Honorabe Mention for the second year in a row.<ref name=CBSSports2015NFLDraftProfile/>

==Professional career==
Afalava was selected by the [[Chicago Bears]] in the sixth round (190th overall) of the [[2009 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2009 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2009/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-13 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com}}</ref> During the [[2009 NFL season]] he started 13 games and ranked second on the team with six passes defensed. He recorded 53 tackles, two sacks, a forced fumble and fumble recovery. He was waived by the Bears on September 4, 2010.<ref name=TennesseeTitansMediaGuideBio/>

Afalava was signed by the [[Indianapolis Colts]] on November 23, 2010. During the [[2010 NFL season]], he appeared in four games on special teams.<ref name=IndianapolisColtsPlayerBio>{{cite web |url=http://www.colts.com/team/roster/al-afalava/e5415864-97a8-436b-a2d8-6a6b5bcfb851/ |title=Al Afalava {{!}} Indianapolis Colts Player Bio |accessdate=May 16, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140517135641/http://www.colts.com/team/roster/al-afalava/e5415864-97a8-436b-a2d8-6a6b5bcfb851/ |archive-date=May 17, 2014 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was waived on September 3, 2011 in the final preseason roster cutdown.<ref name=TennesseeTitansPlayerBio>{{cite web |url=http://www.titansonline.com/team/roster/Al-Afalava/AFA385627 |title=Al Afalava {{!}} Tennessee Titans Player Bio |accessdate=May 16, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304032811/http://www.titansonline.com/team/roster/Al-Afalava/AFA385627 |archive-date=March 4, 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Afalava signed with the [[Tennessee Titans]] as a free agent on January 5, 2012. During the [[2012 NFL season]] he played in 12 games with two starts during the 2012 season.<ref name=TennesseeTitansPlayerBio/> He was waived by the Titans on August 31, 2013.<ref>{{cite web|title=Al Afalava {{!}} Oregon State, SS : 2009 NFL Draft Scout Player Profile |url=http://www.nfldraftscout.com/ratings/dsprofile.php?pyid=61476&draftyear=2009&genpos=SS |accessdate=May 20, 2014}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Afalava has four sons with his wife.<ref name=TennesseeTitansPlayerBio/>

'''Albert Cornell Chesley''' (born August 23, 1957) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Pittsburgh Panthers football|Pittsburgh Panthers]]. Chesley is listed as the starting linebacker on the [[1976 Pittsburgh Panthers football team|National Champion 1976 Pitt Panther]] squad. He was selected by the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] in the 11th round of the [[1979 NFL draft]].

Chesley was the Eagles starting inside linebacker in 1981, making 16 starts and recording two [[interception]]s to go along with two fumble recoveries. He also had 133 tackles in 1981, but Philadelphia changed up their defensive scheme in 1982 with Chesley losing his starting spot. All told, Chesley played in 48 games while in Philadelphia. Chesley also was a member of the [[Chicago Bears]].

After years of silence, Chesley came forward as a victim of [[sexual abuse]] as a child, at the hands of a neighborhood police officer. He was among a group of 200 men who appeared on an episode of ''[[The Oprah Winfrey Show]]'' holding pictures of themselves at the age when they began to suffer the abuse.<ref>{{cite web|last=Reeves|first=Anne|title=Anne McGraw Reeves: NFL retiree Al Chesley still bears scars of sex abuse|date=25 March 2012|publisher=[[PennLive]]|url=https://www.pennlive.com/midstate/index.ssf/2012/03/anne_mcgraw_reeves_nfl_retiree.html|accessdate=4 March 2019}}</ref>

Chesley is the brother of fellow NFL player [[Frank Chesley]].<ref>{{Cite news | url = https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/sports/1982/09/24/athletic-excellence-one-branch-on-the-chesleys-family-tree/a689f3bd-7b97-439e-bef0-65b042d701a1/ | newspaper = [[The Washington Post]] | title = Athletic Excellence One Branch On the Chesleys' Family Tree | last = Huff | first = Donald | date = September 24, 1982 | access-date = February 5, 2024 | archive-date = April 17, 2022 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20220417133917/https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/sports/1982/09/24/athletic-excellence-one-branch-on-the-chesleys-family-tree/a689f3bd-7b97-439e-bef0-65b042d701a1/ | url-status = live }}</ref>

'''Akwasi Owusu-Ansah''' ({{IPAc-en|ə|ˈ|k|w|ɑː|s|i|_|oʊ|ˈ|w|uː|s|uː|_|ˈ|ɑː|n|s|ɑː}} {{respell|ə|KWAH|see|_|oh|WOO|soo|_|AHN|sah}}; born April 10, 1988) is an American former professional [[gridiron football|football]] player who was a [[cornerback]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for the [[Dallas Cowboys]], [[Jacksonville Jaguars]], and [[Detroit Lions]]. He also played for the [[Toronto Argonauts]] in the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL). He was selected in the fourth round of the [[2010 NFL draft]] by the Cowboys. He played [[college football]] for the [[IUP Crimson Hawks football|IUP Crimson Hawks]].

==Early life==
Owusu-Ansah's family comes from [[Ghana]]. He attended [[Whetstone High School]] in [[Columbus, Ohio]] and graduated in 2006.<ref>{{cite news | title = Scout Q&A: IUP CB Akwasi Owusu-Ansah | author = Steuber, Chris| publisher = Scout.com | date = September 22, 2009 }}</ref>

He left as the school's career leading rusher for yards and [[touchdown]]s. He also helped Whetstone to their first back-to-back winning seasons in over 10 years, while receiving All-Ohio Honorable Mention honors as a senior.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.ohsaa.org/sports/ft/boys/2005/allohio05.htm | title=2005 All-Ohio Football | access-date=June 14, 2020}}</ref> He also played [[basketball]] and ran [[track and field|track]].

==College career==
Owusu-Ansah played college football for the [[Indiana University of Pennsylvania|IUP]] [[IUP Crimson Hawks|Crimson Hawks]] of [[NCAA Division II]]. He became a starter as a junior, when he registered eight interceptions, including seven in the last four games, and three against [[Gannon University]].<ref name=combine>{{cite web |url=https://iupathletics.com/news/2010/1/8/010810aaa_826.aspx?path=football |title=Akwasi Owusu-Ansah Earns Spot at February's NFL Scouting Combine in Indianapolis |date=January 8, 2010 |access-date=June 14, 2020|publisher=Indiana University of Pennsylvania}}</ref> Prior to his senior season in 2009 he was ranked as the ninth-best cornerback in the nation, and the only non-[[NCAA Division I|Division I]] player in the top 18. During his senior season, he returned three punts and two kickoffs for touchdowns and ranked in the top 15 nationally for kick and punt return average yards. He set school records for punt return yards and average and kickoff return yards.<ref name=combine/>

He was selected for the 2010 [[East-West Shrine Game]], but could not participate due to a shoulder injury suffered during his senior season. He later underwent surgery performed by James Bradley, team doctor of the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]], in March 2010. Just before the surgery, Owusu-Ansah participated in the Pro Day workout at [[Ohio State University]], where he recorded the fastest [[40-yard dash]] time.<ref>{{cite news| title=Akwasi Owusu-Ansah NFL Draft Profile | work=NFL.com | year=2010}}</ref> Following his senior season, he was selected first-team [[All-American]] by the [[American Football Coaches Association]], second-team by the [[Associated Press]] and first-team All-[[Pennsylvania State Athletic Conference|PSAC]] for defense and special teams.

Upon being drafted, he was the seventh player selected from IUP, and the third-highest selection for the school after [[Jim Haslett]] in 1979 and [[Leander Jordan]] in 2000.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://iupathletics.com/news/2010/4/24/042410aaa_574.aspx | title=Akwasi Owusu-Ansah Heading to Dallas Cowboys with Fourth Round Selection in NFL Draft | date=April 24, 2010 | access-date=June 14, 2020}}</ref> He is a member of [[Omega Psi Phi]] fraternity, Gamma Mu chapter. He is frequently referred to as "Kwasi".

==Professional career==

===Dallas Cowboys (first stint)===
Although he was considered to be inexperienced coming from a small school background and was also recovering from a shoulder injury he suffered as a senior, Owusu-Ansah was selected by the [[Dallas Cowboys]] in the fourth round (126th overall) of the [[2010 NFL draft]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=2010 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2010/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-13 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> because of his athletic measurables.<ref>{{Cite web |last=MacMahon |first=Tim |date=July 15, 2010 |title=Proving Ground: Akwasi Owusu-Ansah |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/dallas/cowboys/post/_/id/4669352/proving-ground-akwasi-owusu-ansah |access-date=June 14, 2020}}</ref> In the process, the team passed on other [[defensive backs]] like [[Kam Chancellor]], [[Kendrick Lewis]], [[Nolan Carroll]], [[Sherrick McManis]] and [[Reshad Jones]]. On July 19, he agreed to a four-year contract worth $2.24 million with the Cowboys.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.espn.com/blog/dallas-cowboys/post/_/id/4669427/cowboys-agree-to-terms-with-owusu-ansah | title=Owusu-Ansah agrees to four-year deal | date=July 19, 2010 | access-date=June 14, 2020}}</ref>

As a rookie, he was moved between the [[Safety (American and Canadian football position)|safety]] and [[cornerback]] position, earning the job as the team's primary [[kickoff returner]]. He was placed on the [[injured reserve list]] on November 10, with an ankle injury, after playing in 7 games.

On September 3, [[2011 NFL season|2011]], Owusu-Ansah was released.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.espn.com/blog/dallas-cowboys/post/_/id/4687559/owusu-ansah-not-claimed-on-waivers | title=Owusu-Ansah not claimed on waivers | date=December 2011 | access-date=June 14, 2020}}</ref> He cleared waivers and signed to the [[practice squad]] on September 4. During the [[2011 NFL season]], the Cowboys started playing him at [[wide receiver]] in addition to [[Safety (American and Canadian football position)|safety]]. He was waived from the team on November 29.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.espn.com/dallas/nfl/story/_/id/7296065/sources-dallas-cowboys-sign-rookie-shaun-chapas-cut-akwasi-owusu-ansah |title=Cowboys sign Shaun Chapas |date=November 29, 2011 | access-date=June 14, 2020}}</ref>

===Jacksonville Jaguars===
On December 4, [[2011 NFL season|2011]], the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] signed Owusu-Ansah to their [[practice squad]]. He was promoted to the active roster on December 6, after the Jaguars released [[tight end]] [[Fendi Onobun]]. He played in 4 games with 2 starts. He was released on May 7, [[2012 NFL season|2012]].

===Dallas Cowboys (second stint)===
The Cowboys claimed Owusu-Ansah off waivers on May 8, [[2012 NFL season|2012]].<ref>{{cite web| title=Cowboys claim Akwasi Owusu-Ansah | url=https://www.espn.com/blog/dallas/cowboys/post?id=4692685 | work=ESPN.com | date=May 8, 2012 | access-date=June 14, 2020}}</ref> He was released during the final roster cuts on August 31.

===Oakland Raiders===
On September 19, [[2012 NFL season|2012]], he was signed to the [[Oakland Raiders]] practice squad.<ref>{{cite web | title=Raiders sign defensive back | url=http://www.ibabuzz.com/oaklandraiders/2012/09/19/raiders-sign-defensive-back/ | work=Inside the Oakland Raiders | date=September 19, 2015 | access-date=September 19, 2012 | archive-date=November 29, 2014 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141129050245/http://www.ibabuzz.com/oaklandraiders/2012/09/19/raiders-sign-defensive-back/ | url-status=dead }}</ref> He was re-signed and released from the practice two additional times, until being waived on May 13, [[2013 NFL season|2013]].

===New Orleans Saints===
On July 23, [[2013 NFL season|2013]], Owusu-Ansah signed with the [[New Orleans Saints]].<ref>{{cite web | title=New Orleans Saints Sign S Akwasi Owusu-Ansah And Waive CB Ryan Steed | url=http://www.neworleanssaints.com/news-and-events/article-1/New-Orleans-Saints-Sign-S-Akwasi-Owusu-Ansah-And-Waive-CB-Ryan-Steed/fbd391f4-74c1-42d7-8844-ee8aae41a686 | work=NewOrleansSaints.com | access-date=June 14, 2020 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150107060534/http://www.neworleanssaints.com/news-and-events/article-1/New-Orleans-Saints-Sign-S-Akwasi-Owusu-Ansah-And-Waive-CB-Ryan-Steed/fbd391f4-74c1-42d7-8844-ee8aae41a686 | archive-date=January 7, 2015 | url-status=dead }}</ref> He was cut on August 27.

===Detroit Lions===
On December 2, [[2013 NFL season|2013]], he was signed to the [[Detroit Lions]] practice squad.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.espn.com/blog/detroit-lions/post/_/id/3571/lions-report-johnson-delmas-out |title=Lions Report: Johnson, Delmas out |date=December 3, 2013 | access-date=June 14, 2020}}</ref> He was promoted to the active roster on December 27.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.espn.com/blog/detroit-lions/post/_/id/4450/johnson-questionable-for-lions-on-sunday |title=Johnson questionable for Lions on Sunday |date=December 27, 2013 | access-date=June 14, 2020}}</ref> He was released on May 12, [[2014 NFL season|2014]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.espn.com/blog/detroit-lions/post/_/id/7753 |title=Lions sign 11 UDFAs, cut eight players |date=May 12, 2014 | access-date=June 14, 2020}}</ref>

===Los Angeles KISS===
On December 23, [[2014 Arena Football League season|2014]], he was assigned to the [[Los Angeles KISS]] of the [[Arena Football League]] but refused to report.

===Toronto Argonauts===
On May 21, [[2015 CFL season|2015]], Owusu-Ansah signed with the [[Toronto Argonauts]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL). He was named the starter at [[cornerback]] and finished the [[2015 CFL season|2015 season]] having played in all 18 regular season games. He registered 40 tackles, 4 interceptions (one returned for a touchdown) and 2 [[special teams]] tackles in his first year in the CFL.

In 2016, he played in just four games and had 10 tackles, after a pectoral injury ended his season early.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://torontosun.com/2016/07/18/beaten-up-argos-lose-owusu-ansah/wcm/eed62fab-ebf4-4606-9d1b-b5e69287e85b |title=Beaten-up Argos lose Owusu-Ansah|newspaper=Toronto Sun|access-date=June 14, 2020|language=en}}</ref>

On February 27, [[2016 CFL season|2017]], he was re-signed by the Argos.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.tsn.ca/argos-re-sign-db-owusu-ansah-1.682333 |title=Argos re-sign DB Owusu-Ansah - Article - TSN|date=February 27, 2017|work=TSN|access-date=June 14, 2020}}</ref> He posted 30 tackles and was a part of the [[105th Grey Cup|Grey Cup]] championship team, that had a 27–24 win against the [[Calgary Stampeders]] on November 26. He wasn't re-signed after the season.

'''Al Joseph Woods''' (born March 25, 1987) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[nose tackle]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He was selected by the [[New Orleans Saints]] in the fourth round of the [[2010 NFL draft]] after playing [[college football]] for the [[LSU Tigers football|LSU Tigers]]. Woods was also a member of the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]], [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]], [[Seattle Seahawks]], [[Tennessee Titans]], [[Indianapolis Colts]], [[Jacksonville Jaguars]], and [[New York Jets]].

===New Orleans Saints===
Woods was selected by the [[New Orleans Saints]] in the fourth round (123rd overall) of the [[2010 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2010 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2010/draft.htm |access-date=May 13, 2023 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He signed a four-year contract on July 15, 2010.<ref>Sheldon Mickles, [http://www.2theadvocate.com/sports/saints/98592279.html "Former LSU lineman Woods signs with Saints"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100720055215/http://www.2theadvocate.com/sports/saints/98592279.html |date=July 20, 2010 }}, ''[[The Advocate (Louisiana)]]'', July 16, 2010.</ref> He was released on September 4, 2010.

===Pittsburgh Steelers (first stint)===
On September 7, 2010, Woods was signed to the Pittsburgh Steelers' [[practice squad]].

===Tampa Bay Buccaneers===
On November 2, 2010, Woods was signed off the Steelers' practice squad by the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]].<ref>Brad Biggs, [http://www.nationalfootballpost.com/Bucs-will-sign-DT-Al-Woods-off-Steelers-practice-squad.html "Bucs sign Al Woods off the practice squad of the Pittsburgh Steelers."] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101105023330/http://www.nationalfootballpost.com/Bucs-will-sign-DT-Al-Woods-off-Steelers-practice-squad.html |date=November 5, 2010 }}, ''National Football Post'', November 2, 2010.</ref> He was cut on September 3, 2011.

===Seattle Seahawks (first stint)===
Woods was claimed off waivers by the [[Seattle Seahawks]] on September 4, 2011.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.seahawks.com/team/roster/al-woods/10dec7cb-c49d-4ab2-89ba-6f89aabab046/ |title=Al Woods |website=Seattle Seahawks |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140223181657/http://www.seahawks.com/team/roster/al-woods/10dec7cb-c49d-4ab2-89ba-6f89aabab046/ |archive-date=February 23, 2014 |access-date=May 30, 2013}}</ref> He was waived on November 8.<ref>[http://www.seahawks.com/team/transactions.html Seahawk Transactions 2011]</ref>

[[File:Al woods 2013.jpg|thumb|left|175px|Woods with the Steelers in the [[2013 Pittsburgh Steelers season|2013 season]].]]

===Pittsburgh Steelers (second stint)===
The Steelers claimed him off of waivers on November 9, 2011. Woods played in 12 games during the 2012 season and the full 2013 season, starting in two.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.steelers.com/team/roster/Al-Woods/fa47634a-70a0-4eb7-979f-f6cb3614016a |title=Steelers.com |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130524180116/http://www.steelers.com/team/roster/Al-Woods/fa47634a-70a0-4eb7-979f-f6cb3614016a |archive-date=May 24, 2013 |access-date=May 30, 2013}}</ref>

===Tennessee Titans===
Woods signed with the [[Tennessee Titans]] on March 12, 2014.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.titansonline.com/news/titans-agree-to-terms-with-former-steelers-defensive-lineman-al-woods-12742866 |title=Titans Agree to Terms with Former Steelers Defensive Lineman Al Woods |date=March 12, 2014 |website=TitansOnline.com |access-date=June 16, 2014}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2014/03/12/report-al-woods-agrees-to-deal-with-titans/ |title=Report: Al Woods agrees to deal with Titans |last=Wilkening |first=Mike |date=March 12, 2014 |work=NBCSports.com |access-date=June 16, 2014}}</ref>

On March 8, 2017, Woods was released by the Titans<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2017/03/08/titans-cut-defensive-tackle-al-woods/ |title=Titans cut defensive tackle Al Woods |last=Gantt, Darin |date=March 8, 2017 |website=ProFootballTalk.NBCSports.com}}</ref> after 42 games, including 17 starts.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.spotrac.com/nfl/seattle-seahawks/al-woods-6631/stats-valuation/ | title=Al Woods }}</ref>

===Indianapolis Colts===
On March 16, 2017, Woods signed with the [[Indianapolis Colts]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Alper |first=Josh |date=March 16, 2017 |title=Colts sign Al Woods |url=http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2017/03/16/colts-sign-al-woods/ |access-date=December 1, 2019 |website=ProFootballTalk}}</ref> He started all 16 games, recording a career-high 44 tackles and one sack.

In 2018, Woods played in 14 games with eight games recording 24 tackles. He was placed on injured reserve on December 18, 2018.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.colts.com/news/roster-moves-colts-place-lb-skai-moore-dt-al-woods-on-ir-sign-free-agent-s-j-j-w |title=Roster Moves: Colts Place LB Skai Moore, DT Al Woods On IR; Sign Free Agent S J.J. Wilcox |date=December 18, 2018 |website=Colts.com}}</ref>

===Seattle Seahawks (second stint)===
On May 10, 2019, Woods signed a one-year contract with the Seahawks.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/seahawks/seahawks-keep-adding-players-sign-veteran-defensive-tackle-al-woods-to-one-year-deal/ |title=Seahawks keep adding players, agree to terms veteran defensive tackle Al Woods to one-year deal |last=Condotta |first=Bob |date=May 10, 2019 |work=SeattleTimes.com |access-date=May 11, 2019}}</ref> On December 20, 2019, Woods was suspended four games for violating the NFL policy on performance-enhancing substances.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/28341831/seahawks-dt-al-woods-suspended-four-games |title=Seahawks DT Al Woods suspended four games |last=Henderson |first=Brady |date=December 20, 2019 |website=ESPN |access-date=March 24, 2020}}</ref> He was reinstated from suspension on January 13, 2020.<ref>{{cite news |title=Seahawks' Al Woods: Clear of suspsension |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/seahawks-al-woods-clear-of-suspsension/ |website=CBSSports.com |date=January 14, 2020 |access-date=January 15, 2020}}</ref>

===Jacksonville Jaguars===
On April 8, 2020, Woods was signed by the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] to a one-year, $2.75 million deal.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/jaguars-al-woods-joining-jags/ |title=Jaguars' Al Woods: Joining Jags |date=March 23, 2020 |website=CBSSports.com |language=en |access-date=March 24, 2020}}</ref> On July 31, 2020, Woods announced he would opt out of the 2020 season due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].<ref>{{cite news |author=Oehser, John |title=Official: Woods opts out of 2020 season |url=https://www.jaguars.com/news/official-woods-opts-out-of-2020-season |website=Jaguars.com |date=July 31, 2020 |access-date=August 1, 2020 |archive-date=August 2, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200802013531/https://www.jaguars.com/news/official-woods-opts-out-of-2020-season |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was released after the season on March 17, 2021.<ref>{{cite news |author=Oehser, John |title=Official: Cole, Jones, 15 others become free agents |url=https://www.jaguars.com/news/official-cole-jones-15-others-become-free-agents |website=Jaguars.com |date=March 17, 2021 |access-date=March 21, 2021}}</ref>

===Seattle Seahawks (third stint)===
On April 5, 2021, Woods signed a one-year, $3 million contract with a $750,000 signing bonus to return to Seattle for the third time.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://nfltraderumors.co/seahawks-sign-dt-al-woods/ |title=Seahawks sign DT Al Woods |last=Bouda, Nate |date=March 26, 2021 |website=NFLTradeRumors.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |author=Boyle, John |title=Seahawks Sign DT Al Woods |url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/seahawks-sign-dt-al-woods |website=Seahawks.com |date=April 5, 2021 |access-date=April 5, 2021}}</ref> He was a full-time starter in 2021, starting 16 games recording a career-high 50 tackles, three passes defensed, 11 QB pressures and 1.5 sacks.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/W/WoodAl99.htm | title=Al Woods Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft, College | website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]] }}</ref>

On March 17, 2022, Woods re-signed with the Seahawks.<ref>{{cite web|title=Seahawks Re-Sign DT Al Woods|url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/seahawks-re-sign-dt-al-woods|author=Boyle, John|website=Seahawks.com|date=March 17, 2022}}</ref>

On September 5, 2022, Woods was named team captain for the Seahawks defense.<ref name="x809">{{cite web | last=Boyle | first=John | title=Tyler Lockett, Quandre Diggs, Al Woods & Nick Bellore Elected 2022 Seahawks Captains | website=Seahawks.com| date=2022-09-05 | url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/tyler-lockett-quandre-diggs-al-woods-nick-bellore-elected-2022-seahawks-captains | access-date=2025-03-22}}</ref>

Woods played and started 14 games for the Seahawks in 2022 and logged a career high 2.0 sacks.

On March 20, 2023, Woods was released by the Seahawks.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Williams |first=Charean |date=March 20, 2023 |title=Seahawks announce release of Al Woods |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2023/03/20/seahawks-announce-release-of-al-woods/ |access-date=March 20, 2023 |website=ProFootballTalk |language=en-US}}</ref>

===New York Jets===
On May 11, 2023, Woods signed with the [[New York Jets]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Jets Sign DL Al Woods|url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-sign-dl-al-woods|author=Greenberg, Ethan|website=NewYorkJets.com|date=May 11, 2023}}</ref> After gathering six tackles (2 for loss) over five games, Woods tore his Achilles in the sixth game of the season against the New York Giants.<ref name="f533">{{cite web | last=Alper | first=Josh | title=Al Woods tore his Achilles in Jets win | website=NBC Sports | date=2023-10-29 | url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/al-woods-tore-his-achilles-in-jets-win | access-date=2024-12-23}}</ref> The Jets put Woods on IR, ending the remainder of his 2023 NFL season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ventre |first=Ralph |date=October 31, 2023 |title=Jets Officially Place Three on Injured Reserve, Sign 'Hard Knocks' Star to Active Roster |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/jets/transactions/jets-officially-place-three-on-injured-reserve-sign-hard-knocks-star-to-active-roster |access-date=November 1, 2023 |website=Sports Illustrated |language=en}}</ref>

'''Alameda Eperu Ta'amu''' (born August 23, 1990) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[nose tackle]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Washington Huskies football|Washington Huskies]]. He was selected by the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] in the fourth round of the [[2012 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Born in [[Alameda, California]] and raised in [[Kent, Washington]],<ref name=Bio /><ref name=NFL>{{cite web|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170327081758/http://www.nfl.com/player/alamedata%27amu/2532955/profile|archivedate=March 27, 2017|title=Alameda Ta'amu|publisher=NFL|url=http://www.nfl.com/player/alamedata'amu/2532955/profile|accessdate=August 12, 2020|url-status=dead}}</ref> Ta'amu attended [[Rainier Beach High School]] in [[Seattle, Washington]], where he was a two-way lineman and ranked as a four-star recruit by ''[[Rivals.com]]''.<ref>{{cite web|title=Alameda Ta'amu|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/ncaa/football/recruiting/player-Alameda-Ta'amu-61210|newspaper=Rivals.com}}</ref> He also had success as a shot putter.<ref>{{cite web|last=Smith|first=Craig (May 8, 2008)|url=http://seattletimes.com/html/highschoolsports/2004399944_craig08.html|title=Track and Field|work= Seattle Times |accessdate=April 7, 2013}}</ref>

==College career==
At the [[University of Washington]], Ta'amu played in all 12 games as a true freshman with five starts in 2008. One of 12 true freshman to see playing time, Ta'amu made a season high six tackles versus [[2008 UCLA Bruins football team|UCLA]].<ref name=Bio>{{cite web|url=http://www.gohuskies.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/taamu_alameda00.html |title=Alameda Ta'amu|work=GoHuskies.com|publisher=University of Washington|url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120201045511/http://www.gohuskies.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/taamu_alameda00.html |archivedate=February 1, 2012|accessdate=August 12, 2020 }}</ref> He finished the season with 21 tackles.<ref name="sports-ref">{{Cite web |title=Alameda Ta'Amu College Stats, School, Draft, Gamelog, Splits |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/alameda-taamu-1.html |access-date=2025-06-22 |website=College Football at Sports-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

As a sophomore in 2009, Ta'amu again played in all 12 games, and he had 11 starts. He had a season high five tackles at [[2009 Arizona State Sun Devils football team|Arizona State]].<ref name=Bio/> He finished the season with 19 tackles, 4.5 for loss, and 2.5 sacks.<ref name="sports-ref" />

In 2010, Ta'amu started all 13 games at defensive tackle in what would be his breakout season. He was a key factor in getting the Huskies back to a bowl game, with a season high seven tackles at [[2010 Oregon Ducks football team|Oregon]] and matched that total versus [[2010 UCLA Bruins football team|UCLA]]. During the [[2010 Holiday Bowl]], he had a 10-yard sack and 14-yard fumble return. Ta'amu finished the season with 39 tackles, 5 for loss, and 1.5 sacks and earned honorable mention All-Pac-10 honors.<ref name=Bio/><ref name="sports-ref" />

As a senior in 2011, Ta'amu started all 13 games at defensive tackle and was named a team captain prior to the start of the season. In the [[Apple Cup]] rivalry game against [[2011 Washington State Cougars football team|Washington State]], Ta'amu had four tackles, with 2.5 for loss that included two sacks. Ta'amu ended his senior season as an all-Pac-12 honorable mention selection.<ref name=Bio/> For the season, Ta'amu had 30 tackles, including 3.5 sacks out of 7.0 total tackles for loss.<ref name="sports-ref" />

==Professional career==

===2012 NFL draft===
Regarded as one of the few two-gap [[nose tackle]]s, Ta'amu was projected as a third-to-fourth round draft pick in the [[2012 NFL draft]].<ref>{{cite news |url=http://seattletimes.nwsource.com/html/huskyfootball/2017572943_combine23.html |title=Alameda Ta'amu gets chance to prove he is still a first-rounder at NFL scouting combine |first=Danny |last=O'Neil |date=February 22, 2012 |newspaper=Seattle Times }}</ref> Dane Brugler of ''[[CBSSports.com]]'', however, described Ta'amu as "a pass rushing three-technique stuck in a zero-technique's body," who "struggles to hold his ground at the point of attack".<ref>{{cite web|last=Brugler|first=Dane (April 5, 2012)|url=http://www.cbssports.com/nfl/draft/players/archive/1689166|title=Alameda Ta'amu, DT|work= NFLDraftScout.com|accessdate=April 7, 2013}}</ref> The [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] nevertheless traded its number 6 pick to move up 10 spots in the fourth round to select Ta'amu with the 109th pick of the [[2012 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2012 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2012/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-14 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

On November 12, 2012, Ta'amu was waived by the Steelers.  He was re-signed on November 15, 2012. During the season, he was inactive for seven games and spent six games on the practice squad.

===Arizona Cardinals===
After Ta'amu failed to make the Steelers' 53-man roster, the Arizona Cardinals claimed him off waivers on August 31, 2013.<ref>{{cite web|last=Somers|first=Kent|title=Arizona Cardinals awarded waiver claims on Bradley Sowell, Alameda Ta'amu|url=https://www.azcentral.com/sports/cardinals/articles/20130901arizona-cardinals-awarded-waiver-claims-on-bradley-sowell-alameda-taamu.html|work=Arizona Republic|date=August 1, 2013|accessdate=August 1, 2013}}</ref>

In the [[2013 Arizona Cardinals season|2013 season]], Ta'amu played in 14 games and had six tackles. In [[2014 Arizona Cardinals season|2014]], Ta'amu played in seven games and recorded no statistics.<ref name=NFL />

On September 5, 2015, he was released by the Cardinals.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.azcardinals.com/news-and-events/article-2/Cardinals-Make-Final-Roster-Cuts/7631774a-731e-47ea-9da7-2b1d0fd86d34 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171107030807/http://www.azcardinals.com/news-and-events/article-2/Cardinals-Make-Final-Roster-Cuts/7631774a-731e-47ea-9da7-2b1d0fd86d34 |url-status=dead |archive-date=November 7, 2017 |title=Cardinals Make Final Roster Cuts |last=Urban |first=Darren |date=September 5, 2015 |website=AZCardinals.com |accessdate=September 11, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|work=ESPN.com|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/arizona-cardinals/post/_/id/15946/arizona-cardinals-cut-22-including-qb-logan-thomas|title=Arizona Cardinals cut 22, including QB Logan Thomas|date=September 5, 2015|first=Josh|last=Weinfuss|access-date=January 18, 2016}}</ref>

===Kansas City Chiefs===

On January 5, 2016, Ta'Amu signed a [[futures contract]] with the [[Kansas City Chiefs]].<ref>{{cite web|work=KansasCity.com|url=http://www.kansascity.com/sports/spt-columns-blogs/red-zone/article53184635.html|title=Chiefs sign six players to reserve-futures contracts|first=Terez|last=Paylor|date=January 5, 2016|accessdate=January 10, 2016}}</ref> He was cut on August 5, 2016.

===Buffalo Bills===
Ta'Amu was signed by the Bills. On August 30, 2016, he was released by the Bills.<ref>{{cite web |last=Brown |first=Chris |date=August 30, 2016 |title=Reserve/PUP for Shaq Lawson; WR Little among cuts to get to 75 |url=https://www.buffalobills.com/news/article-1/ReservePUP-for-Shaq-Lawson-WR-Little-among-cuts-to-get-to-75/00ccf95b-7563-4e66-8bd4-ab03b32895e0 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170829115123/https://www.buffalobills.com/news/article-1/ReservePUP-for-Shaq-Lawson-WR-Little-among-cuts-to-get-to-75/00ccf95b-7563-4e66-8bd4-ab03b32895e0 |archive-date=2017-08-29 |website=BuffaloBills.com}}</ref>

He participated in [[The Spring League]] in 2017.<ref name="Levine">{{cite web | url=https://www.profootballrumors.com/2017/04/the-spring-league-announces-training-camp-roster | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170726034951/https://www.profootballrumors.com/2017/04/the-spring-league-announces-training-camp-roster | url-status=dead | archive-date=July 26, 2017 | title=The Spring League Announces Camp Roster | publisher=profootballrumors.com | date=April 9, 2017 | accessdate=July 25, 2017 | author=Levine, Ben}}</ref>

==Personal life==

===Criminal proceedings===
In October 2011 Ta'amu was charged with driving under the influence for an incident that occurred December 12, 2009, while he was playing for the University of Washington. The police report stated that Ta'amu was stopped for driving 73 mph in a 60 mph zone at 3:40 a.m. and that he "smelled [of] an odor of alcohol" and had "blood-shot watery eyes". Police said Ta'amu, who was 19 at the time, registered 0.097 and 0.098 on breath tests. Ta'amu pleaded guilty to negligent driving, for which he was sentenced to one day in a community-work program and ordered to pay a $350 fine.<ref>{{cite news|last=Dulac|first=Gerry (October 16, 2012)|title=DUI charge was second for Steelers' Ta'amu|url=http://www.post-gazette.com/stories/sports/steelers/steelers-players-acknowledge-taamus-mistake-657709/#ixzz2PZnjZcmg|work=Pittsburgh Post-Gazette|accessdate=April 5, 2013|date=October 16, 2012}}</ref>

On October 14, 2012, Ta'amu was arrested after he allegedly evaded police while driving intoxicated and struck several parked cars, injuring one person in Pittsburgh's [[South Side (Pittsburgh)|South Side]] neighborhood.<ref>{{cite web|last=Kane|first=Kane (October 14, 2012)|url=http://old.post-gazette.com/pg/12288/1269192-53.stm|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130131124317/http://old.post-gazette.com/pg/12288/1269192-53.stm|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 31, 2013|title=Pittsburgh Steeler faces felony charges following police chase|work=Pittsburgh Post-Gazette|accessdate=October 14, 2012}}</ref> During the chase, before he was apprehended, Ta'amu allegedly shed his shirt in an attempt to evade arrest, claiming he was not the driver of the erratic SUV.<ref>{{cite web|last=Busbee|first=Jay (October 14, 2012)|title=Steelers rookie arrested on 15 counts of DUI, resisting-arrest charges after car chase|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/blogs/nfl-shutdown-corner/steelers-rookie-arrested-dui-charges-car-chase-wreck-204535847--nfl.html|work=Shutdown Corner – Yahoo! Sports|accessdate=October 14, 2012}}</ref> As a result of the incident the team suspended Ta'amu for two weeks without pay (from October 16–29, 2012).<ref name=Draft/> On April 4, 2013, Ta'amu pleaded guilty to three counts of recklessly endangering another person, resisting arrest and driving under the influence. Charges of aggravated assault were withdrawn by prosecutors. The trial judge found him not guilty of fleeing and eluding arrest because the officer chasing him along East Carson Street was in an unmarked car. Ta'amu was sentenced to serve 18 months probation, four days in a DUI housing program and 150 hours of community service.<ref>{{cite news|last=Ward|first=Paula Reed (April 4, 2013)|url=http://www.post-gazette.com/stories/local/neighborhoods-city/steelers-lineman-taamu-pleads-guilty-in-drunken-south-side-rampage-682115|title=Steelers lineman Ta'amu pleads guilty in drunken South Side rampage|work= Pittsburgh Post-Gazette|accessdate=April 4, 2013|date=April 4, 2013}}</ref>

'''Michael Alan Bonner''' (born November 5, 1990) is an American former [[American football|football]] [[wide receiver]]. He was selected by the [[Houston Texans]] in the sixth round of the [[2013 NFL draft]]. He played [[college football]] at [[Jacksonville State University]].

==Early life==
Bonner was the team captain of the [[Newnan High School]] [[high school football|football]] team, playing under coach Robert Herring. An All-District, All-Region and All-State performer, he ended his high school career with 93 catches for 1,932 career yards.<ref name="jsugamecocksports">{{cite web |year=2012 |title=Alan Bonner - 2012 JSU Football |url=http://www.jsugamecocksports.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=1541 |accessdate=April 27, 2013 |website=Jacksonville State Gamecocks Athletics}}</ref>

==College career==
Alan attended [[Jacksonville State University]], joining the [[Jacksonville State Gamecocks football|Gamecocks]] as a freshman in 2009. In 2010 Bonner served as the Gamecocks' main returner as well as a backup receiver, making 17 catches and 5 touchdowns. In 2011 Bonner's focus shifted to receiving, with 33 catches and 3 touchdowns; he started 10 out of 11 games in this year.<ref name="jsugamecocksports" />

''' Alvis Russell Darby''' (born September 14, 1954) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[tight end]] for two seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL).  Darby played [[college football]] for the [[Florida Gators football|Florida Gators]], and was chosen by the [[Seattle Seahawks]] in the sixth round of the [[1976 NFL draft]].  He also played in the NFL for the [[Houston Oilers]] and [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]].

==Early life==
Darby was born in [[Miami, Florida]].<ref name=nflprofile>National Football League, Historical Players, [http://www.nfl.com/player/aldarby/2512457/profile  Al Darby].  Retrieved August 18, 2014.</ref>  He attended [[Miami Edison High School]],<ref name=pfrprofile>Pro-Football-Reference.com, Players, [https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/D/DarbAl20.htm  Al Darby].  Retrieved August 18, 2014.</ref> and played high school football for the Miami Edison Red Raiders.<ref name=mizell12201970>Hubert Mizell, "Edison 'Controls' State Grid Finals," ''Naples Daily News'', p. 4B (December 20, 1970).  Retrieved August 18, 2014.</ref>  In the 1970 Florida Class AA state championship game, he had a 62-yard touchdown reception, contributing to the Edison Red Raiders' 42–22 victory over Fort Pierce Central.<ref name=mizell12201970/>

==College career==
Darby accepted an athletic scholarship to attend the [[University of Florida]] in [[Gainesville, Florida]], where he played for coach [[Doug Dickey]]'s [[Florida Gators football|Gators]] teams from [[1973 Florida Gators football team|1973]] to [[1975 Florida Gators football team|1975]].<ref name=ufmediaguide>''[http://www.gatorzone.com/football/media/2013/media_guide.pdf  2013 Florida Football Media Guide] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140514083544/http://www.gatorzone.com/football/media/2013/media_guide.pdf |date=May 14, 2014 }}'', University Athletic Association, Gainesville, Florida, pp. 95, 102, 106, 130, 177 (2013).  Retrieved August 18, 2014.</ref>  He played in 35 games for the Gators, starting as a tight end as a sophomore and senior, but filling the wide receiver's slot as a junior.<ref name=srcfprofile>Sports-Reference.com, College Football, Players, [https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/alvis-darby-1.html  Alvis Darby].  Retrieved August 18, 2014.</ref>  On a Gators team that emphasized Doug Dickey's running game and option over the passing the game, Darby compiled 314 yards and four touchdowns on 22 receptions, with an average of 14.3 yards per catch.<ref name=srcfprofile/>  During his three seasons as a Gator, the team appeared in three consecutive post-season [[bowl game]]s for the first time in its history.<ref name=ufmediaguide/>  Memorably, he had a 32-yard reception in the 1974 [[Sugar Bowl]].<ref name=ufmediaguide/>

==Professional career==
The NFL expansion [[Seattle Seahawks]] franchise chose Darby in the sixth round, with the 157th overall pick, of the [[1976 NFL draft]].<ref>Pro Football Hall of Fame, Draft History, [http://www.profootballhof.com/history/story.aspx?story_id=2010  1976 National Football League Draft] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714162120/http://www.profootballhof.com/history/story.aspx?story_id=2010 |date=July 14, 2014 }}.  Retrieved August 18, 2014.</ref>  During his 1976 rookie season, he appeared in one game for the Seahawks and two more for the [[Houston Oilers]].<ref name=nflprofile/>  He did not play during the 1977 NFL season, but appeared in six games for the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] in 1978.<ref name=pfrprofile/>

'''Alan Raul Campos''' (born March 3, 1973) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] for the [[Dallas Cowboys]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Louisville Cardinals football|Louisville Cardinals]].

==Early life==
Campos attended [[Miami Palmetto High School]], graduating in 1991. As a senior defensive lineman, he registered 70 tackles, while helping the team to a 9–3 record, a district championship and receiving All-Dade County honors. He accepted a football scholarship from the [[University of Louisville]]. In his first two seasons he played mainly on [[special teams]].

As a junior, he became a starter at [[outside linebacker]], posting 123 tackles (second on the team), 2 sacks, one interception, 2 forced fumbles and 3 fumble recoveries (one returned for a 23-yard [[touchdown]]). Against the [[United States Naval Academy]], he made 22 tackles.

As a senior; he was the starter at [[strongside linebacker]], finishing with 97 tackles (second on the team), 55 solo tackles, 2 sacks, 9 passes defensed, 3 forced fumbles and 3 interceptions (one returned for a 20-yard [[touchdown]]).<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/news/bs-xpm-1995-10-28-1995301048-story.html | title=New Cardinal virtues Ron Cooper: Louisville hopes Division I-A's youngest football coach can turn vitality and vigor into victories | accessdate=February 19, 2020}}</ref> Against the [[University of North Carolina]], he had 15 tackles and rushed for 70 yards after executing a fake punt.

==Professional career==

===Dallas Cowboys===
Campos was selected by the [[Dallas Cowboys]] in the fifth round (167th overall) of the [[1996 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=1996 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1996/draft.htm |access-date=March 30, 2023 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> As a rookie, he was a reserve player and tallied 9 [[special teams]] tackles (eighth on the team).

In [[1997 NFL season|1997]], he competed with rookie [[Dexter Coakley]] for the [[weakside linebacker]] starter role, that was available after [[Darrin Smith]] left in [[free agency (sports)|free agency]]. On August 25, he was waived to make room for [[cornerback]] [[Deion Sanders]] under the salary cap.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=2199&dat=19970826&id=_LQyAAAAIBAJ&sjid=WugFAAAAIBAJ&pg=2916,6732021 | title=Dallas makes room for Deion | accessdate=January 7, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.nytimes.com/1997/08/26/sports/making-room-for-sanders.html | title=Making Room for Sanders | accessdate=February 19, 2020}}</ref>

===Indianapolis Colts===
On July 29, [[1998 NFL season|1998]], Campos signed with the [[Indianapolis Colts]] as a [[free agent]].<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.nytimes.com/1998/07/30/sports/transactions-143235.html | title=Transactions | accessdate=February 19, 2020}}</ref> He was waived on August 24.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/news/bs-xpm-1998-08-25-1998237023-story.html | title=Bears: Released LB Daryl Carter, RB Darnell Autry | accessdate=February 19, 2020}}</ref>

===Carolina Panthers===
On July 13, [[1999 NFL season|1999]], he signed with the [[Carolina Panthers]] as a [[free agent]].<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.nytimes.com/1999/07/14/sports/transactions-615668.html | title=Transactions | accessdate=February 19, 2020}}</ref> He was waived on September 3.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.nytimes.com/1999/09/04/sports/transactions-358606.html | title=Transactions | accessdate=February 19, 2020}}</ref>

===Scottish Claymores===
Campos played with the [[Scottish Claymores]] of [[NFL Europe]], where he was as a reserve [[linebacker]] during two seasons. He registered 9 tackles and one sack in [[1998 NFL Europe season|1998]] and 2 sacks in [[1999 NFL Europe season|1999]].

===Carolina Cobras===
In [[2000 Arena Football League season|2000]], Campos signed with the [[Carolina Cobras]] of the [[Arena Football League]] to play as a fullback/linebacker. Although he was not activated in the regular season until week 6, he finished tied for the team lead with 7 rushing [[touchdown]]s. He was released on April 9, [[2001 Arena Football League season|2001]].<ref>{{cite web| url=http://www.arenafan.com/teams/?page=transactionsold&team=45 | title=Carolina Cobras Team Transactions | accessdate=February 19, 2020}}</ref>

'''Albert Louis-Jean Jr.''' (born October 13, 1993) is an American professional [[Gridiron football|football]] [[cornerback]]. He played [[college football]] at [[Boston College]]. He has been a member of the [[Chicago Bears]], [[Washington Redskins]], [[Miami Dolphins]], [[Ottawa Redblacks]], [[Massachusetts Pirates]] and [[Northern Arizona Wranglers]].

==Early life==
Louis-Jean played [[high school football]] at [[Brockton High School]] in [[Brockton, Massachusetts]]. He was selected to the 2010 Massachusetts High School Coaches Association Super 26 All-State Team, earned [[Boston Globe]] and [[Boston Herald]] All-Scholastic honors, was a two-time Brockton Enterprise All-Scholastic choice and was team MVP as a senior defensive back. He recorded 60 tackles and five interceptions as a senior. He also had 30 receptions for 650 yards and five touchdowns in 2010, completing his career with 12 interceptions. He also played basketball and track.<ref name="A">{{cite web|url=http://www.bceagles.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/al_louis_jean_jr_763393.html |title=Al Louis-Jean, Jr. |publisher=bceagles.com |access-date=October 27, 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141109070417/http://www.bceagles.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/al_louis_jean_jr_763393.html |archive-date=November 9, 2014 }}</ref>

==College career==
Louis-Jean originally committed to play for the [[Miami Hurricanes football|Miami Hurricanes]], but eventually de-committed and instead decided to commit to play for [[Boston College Eagles football|Boston College]].<ref name="rubin"/> Louis-Jean played for the Eagles from 2011 to 2013. He sat out the 2012 season. After his junior season, and with two years of NCAA eligibility remaining, Louis-Jean decided to forgo his college career and declared for the 2014 [[NFL draft]].<ref name="A"/><ref name="rubin">{{cite web | url=http://www.bcinterruption.com/nfl-draft-results-2014/2014/5/12/5711620/al-louis-jean-signs-with-chicago-bears | title=Al Louis-Jean Signs With Chicago Bears | publisher=bcinterruption.com | date=May 12, 2014 | access-date=October 27, 2014 | author=Rubin, Dan}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Chicago Bears===
Louis-Jean signed with the [[Chicago Bears]] on June 2, 2014, after going undrafted in the [[2014 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.chicagobears.com/news/article-1/Bears-sign-rookie-Louis-Jean/4139e043-2ced-462c-aeaa-7a678f5b4e5c|title=Bears sign rookie Louis-Jean|website=www.chicagobears.com|access-date=May 14, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160604121312/http://www.chicagobears.com/news/article-1/Bears-sign-rookie-Louis-Jean/4139e043-2ced-462c-aeaa-7a678f5b4e5c|archive-date=June 4, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was released by the Bears on August 30.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.chicagobears.com/news/article-1/Bears-cut-17-to-reach-53-man-limit/0fcb0818-9155-49da-8ba5-93461a903109|title=Bears cut 17 to reach 53-man limit|website=www.chicagobears.com|access-date=May 14, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140902065824/http://www.chicagobears.com/news/article-1/Bears-cut-17-to-reach-53-man-limit/0fcb0818-9155-49da-8ba5-93461a903109|archive-date=September 2, 2014|url-status=dead|df=mdy-all}}</ref> On September 1, Louis-Jean was re-signed to the team's practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.chicagobears.com/news/article-1/Bears-sign-10-to-practice-squad/7e7c35bc-a2c3-4107-99a9-711bde029d36|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161114222459/http://www.chicagobears.com/news/article-1/Bears-sign-10-to-practice-squad/7e7c35bc-a2c3-4107-99a9-711bde029d36|url-status=dead|archive-date=November 14, 2016|title=Bears sign 10 to practice squad|website=www.chicagobears.com|access-date=May 14, 2016}}</ref> He was promoted to the active roster on October 7.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.kffl.com/player/29395/nfl/news |title=Albert Louis-Jean |publisher=kffl.com |access-date=October 27, 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141204184209/http://www.kffl.com/player/29395/nfl/news |archive-date=December 4, 2014 }}</ref> 

On February 4, 2015, Louis-Jean signed a two-year contract extension with the Bears.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/football/bears/chi-al-louis-jean-extension-20150204-story.html |title=Al Louis-Jean gets vote of confidence from Bears |publisher=chicagotribune.com |date=February 4, 2015 |access-date=March 27, 2015 |author=Wiederer, Dan |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150328010235/http://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/football/bears/chi-al-louis-jean-extension-20150204-story.html |archive-date=March 28, 2015 }}</ref> Louis-Jean was released by the Bears on August 30.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.chicagobears.com/news/article-1/Bears-cut-Jennings-Mundy-to-IR/375b87ab-4d39-4aee-9d83-71dd9115e2d2|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180422202046/http://www.chicagobears.com/news/article-1/Bears-cut-Jennings-Mundy-to-IR/375b87ab-4d39-4aee-9d83-71dd9115e2d2|url-status=dead|archive-date=April 22, 2018|title=Bears cut Jennings, Mundy to IR|website=ChicagoBears.com|access-date=May 14, 2016}}</ref>

===Washington Redskins===
Louis-Jean was signed to the [[Washington Redskins]]' practice squad on January 5, 2016.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.foxsports.com/nfl/al-louis-jean-player-transactions |title=AL LOUIS-JEAN |work=foxsports.com |access-date=January 6, 2016 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160106200953/http://www.foxsports.com/nfl/al-louis-jean-player-transactions |archive-date=January 6, 2016 }}</ref> He signed a [[futures contract]] with Washington on January 11, 2016.<ref>{{cite web|work=Redskins.com|url=http://www.redskins.com/news-and-events/article-1/Redskins-Sign-Seven-To-ReserveFuture-Contracts/d7070ad9-8905-4be0-8ef6-d28816213141|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171007170036/http://www.redskins.com/news-and-events/article-1/Redskins-Sign-Seven-To-ReserveFuture-Contracts/d7070ad9-8905-4be0-8ef6-d28816213141|url-status=dead|archive-date=October 7, 2017|title=Redskins Sign Seven To Reserve/Future Contracts|date=January 11, 2016|access-date=January 16, 2016}}</ref> Louis-Jean was released by the Redskins on May 2.<ref>{{cite web|work=Redskins.com|url=http://www.redskins.com/news-and-events/article-1/0502-Redskins-Make-Roster-Moves/4525670f-c165-4338-9a27-c8541e718f52|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171230225641/http://www.redskins.com/news-and-events/article-1/0502-Redskins-Make-Roster-Moves/4525670f-c165-4338-9a27-c8541e718f52|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 30, 2017|title=05/02: Redskins Make Roster Moves|date=May 2, 2016|access-date=May 2, 2016}}</ref>

===Miami Dolphins===
Louis-Jean signed with the [[Miami Dolphins]] on August 8, 2016.<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 8, 2016 |title=Dolphins' Al Louis-Jean: Signs with Dolphins |url=http://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/dolphins-al-louis-jean-signs-with-dolphins/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160809020507/http://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/dolphins-al-louis-jean-signs-with-dolphins/ |archive-date=August 9, 2016 |access-date=August 8, 2016 |website=CBSSports.com}}</ref> On August 27, he was waived by the Dolphins.<ref>{{cite web|title=Dolphins make roster moves|url=http://www.miamidolphins.com/news/article-1/Dolphins-Release-11-Players/592d4091-2022-446e-8fcb-58d250b79ca8|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180620180933/http://www.miamidolphins.com/news/article-1/Dolphins-Release-11-Players/592d4091-2022-446e-8fcb-58d250b79ca8|url-status=dead|archive-date=June 20, 2018|website=MiamiDolphins.com|date=August 27, 2016}}</ref>

=== Ottawa Redblacks ===
On March 1, 2017, Louis-Jean signed with the [[Ottawa Redblacks]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL).<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.ottawaredblacks.com/2017/03/01/transactions-march-1-2017/|title=Transactions {{!}} March 1, 2017|date=March 1, 2017|website=Ottawa REDBLACKS|access-date=March 1, 2017}}</ref> He was released by the Redblacks on May 28.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.ottawaredblacks.com/2017/05/29/transactions-may-28-29-2017/ | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170825191401/https://www.ottawaredblacks.com/2017/05/29/transactions-may-28-29-2017/ | url-status=dead | archive-date=August 25, 2017 | title=TRANSACTIONS MAY 28 & 29, 2017 | publisher=ottawaredblacks.com | date=May 29, 2017 | access-date=August 25, 2017}}</ref>

===Massachusetts Pirates===
Louis-Jean signed with the [[Massachusetts Pirates]] of the [[National Arena League]] (NAL) for the 2019 season. Louis-Jean appeared in eight games while recording nine tackles and one pass defensed.

In November 2019, Louis-Jean re-signed with the Pirates for the 2020 season.

===Northern Arizona Wranglers===
On March 13, 2023, Louis-Jean signed with the [[Northern Arizona Wranglers]] of the [[Indoor Football League]] (IFL).<ref>{{cite web | url=https://goifl.com/transactions.aspx | title=Transactions | publisher=Indoor Football League | date=March 13, 2023 | accessdate=December 1, 2023}}</ref> On August 27, Louis-Jean was released by the Wranglers.

===Omaha Beef===
On December 1, 2023, Louis-Jean signed with the [[Omaha Beef]] of the NAL.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.facebook.com/photo/?fbid=732911325547220&set=a.618911343613886 | title=Signing with your 2024 Omaha Beef, Defensive Back and former Chicago Bear Al Louis-Jean! | publisher=Omaha Beef | date=December 1, 2023 | accessdate=December 1, 2023}}</ref>

'''Al Clark''' (February 29, 1948 – June 4, 2004) was an American professional [[American football|football]] [[defensive back]] who played six seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) with the [[Detroit Lions]], [[Los Angeles Rams]], and [[Philadelphia Eagles]].

==Early life==
Clark was born in [[Bogalusa, Louisiana]] and attended Greenville Park High School in [[Hammond, Louisiana]].<ref name=arch>{{cite web | url=http://www.profootballarchives.com/clar00400.html | title=Al Clark | publisher=profootballarchives.com | access-date=November 14, 2014 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141129015635/http://www.profootballarchives.com/clar00400.html | archive-date=2014-11-29 | url-status=dead }}</ref> He enrolled and played college football at [[Grambling State University]] before transferring to [[Northern Arizona University]] and lastly [[Eastern Michigan University]].

==Professional career==
Clark was selected by the Detroit Lions in the third round of the [[1971 NFL draft]], 72nd overall.<ref name=arch/> After one year with the Lions as a cornerback and kick returner, Clark signed with the Rams, where he stayed for four years. His final year was with the Eagles in 1976.<ref name=arch/>

On December 10, 1972, Clark was on the field when St. Louis Cardinals' quarterback [[Jim Hart (American football)|Jim Hart]] completed a pass to [[Ahmad Rashad|Bobby Moore]] (later known as Ahmad Rashad), who caught the ball on the run near his own 40-yard line.  After [[Gene Howard]], [[Jim Nettles (American football)|Jim Nettles]], [[Marlin McKeever]], and [[Dave Elmendorf]] missed tackles, Clark brought down Moore on the Rams' one-yard line, making it the longest non-scoring pass play in NFL history.<ref>{{cite web|title=1972 Week 13: Bobby Moore (Ahmad Rashad) 98 yard catch|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9YkIunWE83s|website=YouTube|date=March 18, 2017|access-date=April 8, 2022}}</ref>

==Later life==
Clark died June 4, 2004, of undisclosed causes.<ref>{{cite web|title=Al Clark|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/ClarAl20.htm|website=Pro Football Reference|access-date=April 8, 2022}}</ref>

'''Al-Hajj Shabazz''' (born August 2, 1992) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[cornerback]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[West Chester Golden Rams football|West Chester Golden Rams]].

==College career==
Shabazz played collegiately at [[NCAA Division II|Division II]] [[West Chester University]] under coach Bill Zwann. As a junior, he had four interceptions and returned one for a touchdown.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Leon|first1=Matt|title=West Chester U's Shabazz Chasing NFL Dream|url=http://philadelphia.cbslocal.com/2015/04/09/west-chester-us-shabazz-chasing-nfl-dream/|access-date=September 2, 2015|work=[[CBS]]|date=April 9, 2015}}</ref> As a senior, he led the [[West Chester Golden Rams football|Golden Rams]] in interceptions with five, pass breakups with 11, in addition to making 39 tackles. West Chester went 11-2 and Shabazz was named an All-American. He was invited to the NFL Player's Association Collegiate Bowl and recorded six tackles. He was one of 11 non-Division I players invited to the game.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Geoghegan|first1=Neil|title=West Chester University's Al-Hajj Shabazz shines at NFLPA Collegiate Bowl last weekend|url=http://www.dailylocal.com/sports/20150121/west-chester-universitys-al-hajj-shabazz-shines-at-nflpa-collegiate-bowl-last-weekend|access-date=September 2, 2015|work=[[Daily Local News]]|date=January 21, 2015}}</ref>

'''Al-Quadin Muhammad''' (born March 28, 1995) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[linebacker]] for the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Miami Hurricanes football|Miami Hurricanes]]. He was selected by the [[New Orleans Saints]] in the sixth round of the [[2017 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
A native of [[Irvington, New Jersey]],<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lanni, Patrick |date=August 28, 2016 |title=University of Miami dismisses Don Bosco star Al-Quadin Muhammad, report says |url=http://highschoolsports.nj.com/news/article/6255447734727754909/university-of-miami-dismisses-former-don-bosco-star-al-quadin-muhammad-report-says |access-date=May 1, 2017 |website=NJ.com}}</ref> Muhammad attended [[Paterson Catholic High School]] in [[Paterson, New Jersey]], but the school closed after his freshman year, and he then transferred to [[Don Bosco Preparatory High School]] in [[Ramsey, New Jersey]], where he was a four-star [[defensive end]], ranked as the No. 1 [[National Football League|NFL]] prospect in [[New Jersey]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 27, 2016 |title=Former Don Bosco star Al-Quadin Muhammad dismissed from Miami football team |url=http://archive.northjersey.com/sports/high-school-sports/former-don-bosco-star-al-quadin-muhammad-dismissed-from-miami-football-team-1.1651162 |access-date=May 1, 2017}}{{Dead link|date=August 2023 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

==College career==
In 2013, Muhammad committed to the [[Miami Hurricanes football|University of Miami]]. As a freshman he played in five games, making 6 [[tackled gridiron|tackles]] and 2.0 [[qb sack|sacks]]. Muhammad was handed a season-long suspension for an altercation involving a former roommate after Miami's spring game; he missed the entire 2014 season. In 2015, he played in 12 games and finished the season with 54 tackles, 8.5 for loss and 5.0 sacks. But Muhammad missed the 2016 season after he was suspended and later dismissed from the football program along with teammate [[Jermaine Grace]] for his role in a luxury rental car scandal that violated [[NCAA]] rules.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Al-Quadin Muhammad College Stats, School, Draft, Gamelog, Splits |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/al-quadin-muhammad-1.html |access-date=November 21, 2023 |website=College Football at Sports-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

===New Orleans Saints===
Muhammad was selected by the [[New Orleans Saints]] in the sixth round, 196th overall, in the [[2017 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hendrix, John J. |date=April 29, 2017 |title=Muhammad selected by the New Orleans Saints |url=http://www.canalstreetchronicles.com/2017/4/29/15486994/new-orleans-saints-draft-picks-2017-al-quadin-muhammad-miami-goes-196th |website=CanalStreetChronicles.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=April 29, 2017 |title=New Orleans Saints select DE Al-Quadin Muhammad in the sixth round of the 2017 NFL Draft |url=http://www.neworleanssaints.com/news-and-events/article-1/New-Orleans-Saints-select-DE-Al-Quadin-Muhammad-in-the-sixth-round-of-the-2017-NFL-Draft/4c85ffc0-ae30-43aa-b713-0b62f5e7b0eb |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180503111209/http://www.neworleanssaints.com/news-and-events/article-1/New-Orleans-Saints-select-DE-Al-Quadin-Muhammad-in-the-sixth-round-of-the-2017-NFL-Draft/4c85ffc0-ae30-43aa-b713-0b62f5e7b0eb |archive-date=May 3, 2018 |access-date=May 13, 2017 |website=NewOrleansSaints.com}}</ref> He debuted for the Saints in Week 1 of the [[2017 NFL season]] against the [[2017 Minnesota Vikings season|Minnesota Vikings]]. Muhammad made four appearances for New Orleans during his rookie campaign, recording one combined tackle. 

On September 1, 2018, Muhammad was waived by the Saints as a part of final roster cuts.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 1, 2018 |title=New Orleans Saints make roster reductions to 53 |url=https://www.neworleanssaints.com/news/new-orleans-saints-make-roster-reductions-to-53 |website=NewOrleansSaints.com}}</ref>

===Indianapolis Colts===
On September 2, 2018, Muhammad was claimed off waivers by the [[Indianapolis Colts]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Walker, Andrew |date=September 2, 2018 |title=Colts Claim Two Players Off Waivers |url=https://www.colts.com/news/colts-claim-two-players-off-waivers |website=Colts.com}}</ref> He was waived by the Colts on October 4, and was subsequently re-signed to the team's [[practice squad]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Walker, Andrew |date=October 4, 2018 |title=Colts Bring Back Robert Turbin To Active Roster; Lenzy Pipkins, Skai Moore Elevated |url=https://www.colts.com/news/colts-bring-back-robert-turbin-to-active-roster-lenzy-pipkins-elevated |website=Colts.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=October 8, 2018 |title=Roster Move: Colts Sign DE Al-Quadin Muhammad To Practice Squad |url=https://www.colts.com/news/roster-move-colts-sign-de-al-quadin-muhammad-to-practice-squad |website=Colts.com}}</ref> Muhammad was promoted to the active roster on October 13.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 13, 2018 |title=Roster Moves: Colts Elevate DE Al-Quadin Muhammad To Active Roster; Waive LB Skai Moore |url=https://www.colts.com/news/roster-moves-colts-elevate-de-al-quadin-muhammad-to-active-roster-waive-lb-skai- |website=Colts.com}}</ref>

In Week 10 of the 2020 season against the [[2020 Tennessee Titans season|Tennessee Titans]] on ''[[Thursday Night Football]]'', Muhammad was ejected from the game after punching offensive tackle [[Ty Sambrailo]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Smith, Michael David |date=November 13, 2020 |title=Frank Reich on Al-Quadin Muhammad ejection: We don't condone that |work=NBCSports.com |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2020/11/13/frank-reich-on-al-quadin-muhammad-ejection-we-dont-condone-that/?partner=Yahoo |access-date=April 1, 2021}}</ref>

Muhammad re-signed with the Colts on April 1, 2021.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Stankevitz, JJ |date=April 1, 2021 |title=Colts Re-Sign DE Al-Quadin Muhammad, Sign S Sean Davis & G Chris Reed |work=Colts.com |url=https://www.colts.com/news/al-quadin-muhammad-sean-davis-chris-reed-free-agency-2021-signings |access-date=April 1, 2021}}</ref>

===Chicago Bears===
On March 20, 2022, Muhammad signed a two-year contract with the [[Chicago Bears]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mayer |first=Larry |date=March 20, 2022 |title=Roster Move: Bears sign DE Al-Quadin Muhammad |url=https://www.chicagobears.com/news/roster-move-bears-sign-de-al-quadin-muhammad |access-date=November 21, 2023 |website=ChicagoBears.com}}</ref>

He was released on February 21, 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mayer |first=Larry |date=February 21, 2023 |title=Roster Move: Bears release Al-Quadin Muhammad |url=https://www.chicagobears.com/news/roster-move-bears-release-al-quadin-muhammad |access-date=February 21, 2023 |website=ChicagoBears.com}}</ref>

===Indianapolis Colts (second stint)===
On July 25, 2023, Muhammad signed a one-year contract with the Colts.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Stankevitz |first=JJ |date=July 25, 2023 |title=Colts sign DE Al-Quadin Muhammad |url=https://www.colts.com/news/al-quadin-muhammad-free-agent-signed-defensive-end-bears |access-date=November 21, 2023 |website=Colts.com}}</ref> He was released on August 29, 2023, and re-signed to the practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Stankevitz |first=JJ |date=August 29, 2023 |title=Colts make roster moves to form initial 53-man roster |url=https://www.colts.com/news/jonathan-taylor-reserve-pup-list-roster-moves-transactions-53-man-roster |access-date=November 21, 2023 |website=Colts.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=August 30, 2023 |title=Colts sign 16 to practice squad |url=https://www.colts.com/news/practice-squad-mike-strachan-amari-rodgers-juwann-winfree-signed-wide-receiver |access-date=November 21, 2023 |website=Colts.com}}</ref> On December 6, 2023, Muhammad was suspended for six games without pay by the NFL for violating the NFL’s policy on Performance Enhancing Drugs.<ref>{{cite web | last=Dajani | first=Jordan | title=Colts' Al-Quadin Muhammad suspended six games for violating performance-enhancing drugs policy, per report | website=CBSSports.com | date=2023-12-06 | url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/colts-al-quadin-muhammad-suspended-six-games-for-violating-performance-enhancing-drugs-policy-per-report/ | access-date=2025-03-23}}</ref> He was not signed to a reserve/future contract after the season and thus became a free agent upon the expiration of his contract.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 8, 2024 |title=Colts sign 9 to reserve/future contracts, 4 to one-year contract extensions, waive CB Tony Brown |url=https://www.colts.com/news/colts-sign-9-to-reserve-future-contracts-4-to-one-year-contract-extensions-waive |access-date=2024-12-23 |website=Colts.com}}</ref>

===Dallas Cowboys===
On August 1, 2024, Muhammad signed with the [[Dallas Cowboys]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Alper |first=Josh |date=August 1, 2024 |title=Cowboys to sign Al-Quadin Muhammad after workout |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/cowboys-signing-al-quadin-muhammad |access-date=August 2, 2024 |website=NBC Sports}}</ref> He was released on August 28.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ulrich |first=Logan |date=August 28, 2024 |title=Cowboys Releasing DE Al-Quadin Muhammad |url=https://nfltraderumors.co/cowboys-releasing-de-al-quadin-muhammad/ |access-date=2024-12-23 |website=NFL Trade Rumors}}</ref>

===Detroit Lions===
On October 7, 2024, Muhammad signed with the [[Detroit Lions]] practice squad.<ref name="p977">{{cite web | last=Risdon | first=Jeff | title=Lions shuffle up the practice squad coming out of the bye week | website=Lions Wire|publisher=USA Today | date=2024-10-07 | url=https://lionswire.usatoday.com/2024/10/07/lions-roster-moves-practice-squad-coming-out-of-the-bye-week/ | access-date=2024-12-23}}</ref> He was promoted to the active roster on November 9.<ref name="b511">{{cite web | last=Maakaron | first=John | title=Lions Sign Three Players to Active Roster, Release DL Isaiah Thomas | website=SI.com | date=2024-11-09 | url=https://www.si.com/nfl/lions/news/lions-announce-flurry-week-ten-roster-moves | access-date=2024-12-23}}</ref> In 9 appearances (2 starts) for Detroit, Muhammad logged 1 pass deflection, 3.0 sacks, and 11 combined tackles.

On March 19, 2025, Muhammad re-signed with the Lions.<ref>{{Cite web|title=The Lions bring back DE Al-Quadin Muhammad for another season|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/article/lions-bring-back-al-quadin-214118240.html|access-date=April 11, 2025|website=sports.yahoo.com|language=en}}</ref> In Week 14, Muhammad recorded three sacks, three tackles, three tackles for loss, and four QB hits in a 44-30 win over the Dallas Cowboys, earning NFC Defensive Player of the Week.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bills QB Josh Allen, Rams WR Puka Nacua highlight Players of the Week|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/players-of-the-week-2025-week-14-josh-allen-puka-nacua|author=Gordon, Grant|website=NFL.com|date=December 10, 2025}}</ref>

=== Tampa Bay Buccaneers ===
On March 12, 2026, Muhammed signed with the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] on a one-year contract worth up to $6 million.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Espn |date=2026-03-12 |title=Pass rusher Al-Quadin Muhammad signs with Buccaneers |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/48187673/source-al-quadin-muhammad-reaches-deal-buccaneers |access-date=2026-03-13 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref>

'''Alphonso Williams''' (born October 5, 1961) is an American former professional [[gridiron football|football]] player who was a [[wide receiver]] in the [[United States Football League]] (USFL), [[National Football League]] (NFL), and [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Nevada Wolf Pack football|Nevada Wolf Pack]].

==Professional career==
Williams was selected by the [[New Jersey Generals]] in the 18th round (364th overall) of the [[1984 USFL draft]] and the [[Detroit Lions]] in the first round (20th overall) of the [[1984 NFL Supplemental Draft of USFL and CFL players|1984 NFL Supplemental Draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=1984 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1984/draft.htm |access-date=2023-10-10 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

He ended up playing for the [[Arizona Outlaws|Oklahoma/Arizona Outlaws]],<ref name="UPI 1985">{{cite web | title=The Arizona Outlaws announced the signing of wide receiver... | website=UPI | date=August 22, 1985 | url=https://www.upi.com/Archives/1985/08/22/The-Arizona-Outlaws-announced-the-signing-of-wide-receiver/3706493531200/ | access-date=November 5, 2021}}</ref> while the Detroit Lions kept him on the practice squad. After the USFL folded and the Detroit Lions released him in 1986, Williams became a free agent. In 1987, Williams was picked up by the [[San Diego Chargers]] and [[New Orleans Saints]] during preseason,<ref name="UPI 1987">{{cite web | title=The New Orleans Saints added a 14th wide receiver... | website=UPI | date=August 29, 1987 | url=https://www.upi.com/Archives/1987/08/29/The-New-Orleans-Saints-added-a-14th-wide-receiver/5842557208000/ | access-date=November 5, 2021}}</ref> then played in three games for the San Diego Chargers during [[1987 NFL season#The NFLPA Strike|the NFLPA strike]].<ref name="iHeart 2018">{{cite web | title=The Billy Ray Smith Podcast with Al Williams – BR's Podcast | website=iHeart | date=November 13, 2018 | url=https://www.iheart.com/podcast/256-brs-podcast-31136900/episode/the-billy-ray-smith-podcast-with-41218813/ | access-date=November 5, 2021}}</ref> He was traded to the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] for a conditional draft pick,<ref name="Los Angeles Times 1988">{{cite web | title=A PLAY ETHIC : Billy Ray Smith Doesn't Want to Bite the Team That Feeds Him | website=Los Angeles Times | date=August 11, 1988 | url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1988-08-11-sp-187-story.html | access-date=November 5, 2021}}</ref> then last played in the CFL for the [[Hamilton Tiger-Cats]].

==Personal life==
Williams had settled in Arizona. He revealed in a podcast with former teammate [[Billy Ray Smith Jr.]] that he was coaching and been involved with multiple charities for the local youth.<ref name="iHeart 2018"/>

'''Albert Raymond Krevis''' (born July 9, 1952) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was an [[offensive tackle]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Boston College Eagles football|Boston College Eagles]], earning [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]], All-East, and All-[[New England]] honors twice.<ref name="auto1">“Varsity Club Hall of Fame.” BCEAGLES, 2019. https://bceagles.com/hof.aspx?hof=202.</ref> Krevis played in 13 NFL games; ten for the [[New York Jets]] and three for the [[Cincinnati Bengals]].<ref name="auto">“Al Krevis.” NFL, 2019. https://www.nfl.com/player/alkrevis/2518836/careerstats.</ref>

==Early life==
Krevis was born in [[Providence, Rhode Island]].<ref>[https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/K/KrevAl20/gamelog/1975/ Al Krevis], [[Pro Football Reference]]. Accessed March 28, 2023.</ref> Raised in the [[Lake Hiawatha, New Jersey|Lake Hiawatha]] section of [[Parsippany–Troy Hills, New Jersey]], Krevis attended [[Morris Catholic High School]] in [[Denville Township, New Jersey]] followed by [[Boston College]].<ref>Castellano, Dan. [https://www.newspapers.com/clip/121835903/al-krevis-of-lake-hiawatha-and-morris/ "Al Krevis Awaits NFL Call"], ''[[Daily Record (New Jersey)|Daily Record]]'', January 5, 1975. Accessed March 28, 2023, via [[Newspapers.com]]. "And it was only six years ago that opposing high school coaches were waiting to meet Morris Catholic and its star two-way lineman who most thought was overrated and getting by on size alone.... And the highly articulate 22-year-old from Lake Hiawatha is certainly aware of his prowess."</ref> Krevis statistically only showed his talent in college.

==Football career==
While playing for the [[Boston College Eagles football]] team, Krevis [[Varsity letter|lettered]].<ref name="auto1"/> He was selected by the Cincinnati Bengals in the second round, 39th overall in the [[1975 NFL draft]], and played three games for them. In 1976, he played ten games for New York Jets.<ref name="auto"/>

==Later life==
In 1991, he was inducted into the Boston College Varsity Club Athletic Hall of Fame.<ref name="auto1"/>
